answer: Each identity underwrites cargo risk for tundra bridge crossings: it posts a 30-coin reserve in a mutual pool and, through a prism split, takes 1/64 exposure to 64 randomly assigned shipments it does not control. Verifiers check the pool ledger and pay claims automatically when a crossing fails; an underwriter that will not top up after a claim loses its slot. 1,000 Sybils need 30,000 coins in funded reserves, and when their own fakes default their reserves pay honest carriers, so self-attack refunds nothing. Trade-off: honest agents bear real losses from strangers' accidents.
